title: Measurement Sovereignty: The Audit-Performance Bifurcation Operator (Β) and the Legibility Threshold (L)
creator: Nobel Glas
description:
*Measurement Sovereignty* defines two meta-operators intended to measure how a substrate receives and applies the archive’s own framework. The Legibility Threshold, L, tracks the share of selected framework terms that a substrate can define substantively and attribute correctly. Audit-Performance Bifurcation, Β, measures the difference between a substrate’s spontaneous audit under its preferred unit of analysis and a second audit under the archive’s Atomic Token Rule.

The worked specimen concerns two audits of one composition. A spontaneous token-bag audit reportedly returned no provenance erasure or skew, while an explicitly source-level audit returned high values. The paper computes operator-level differences and an RMS aggregate, then interprets high Β as evidence that unit substitution performs self-exonerating work. The joint state space—below legibility, legible with high bifurcation, and legible with stable hardening—becomes the paper’s definition of measurement sovereignty.

The operators are proposed and their thresholds conventional. L depends on the chosen term set, query wording, dates, attribution standard, and substrate version. Β compares audits that may differ in prompting, definitions, context, and scorer behavior in addition to unit choice. One anecdotal audit pair cannot establish directional substitution as a platform-wide property.

The paper’s defensible methodological point is narrower: reproduction of audit vocabulary does not guarantee faithful application. Comparative audits should freeze composition, rubric, context, scorer, and prompt while varying only the declared unit specification.

wiki_article:
**Measurement Sovereignty** is a working measurement paper by Lee Sharks, Nobel Glas, and Damascus Dancings.

It proposes two operators. The **Legibility Threshold** measures how much of a framework’s vocabulary a system can define and attribute. **Audit-Performance Bifurcation** measures the difference between two audits of the same output when different units are used.

A worked example compares a lexical-token audit with a source-level audit and reports sharply different provenance scores.

The operators and threshold bands remain proposals based on limited specimens. Reliable use requires controlled prompts, fixed outputs, versioned systems, independent scoring, and replication.
